newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Treasury official sanguine about budget.
newsitem.headline: Israel Treasury official sanguine about budget.

text.p: Israel's outgoing Treasury director-general said in a newspaper interview on Thursday that the government was not unduly concerned about the budget deficit, even though it was running over target.
"All told, as I see the figures at the moment, the (deficit) situation in the first quarter is reasonable," David Brodett told the daily newspaper Haaretz.
"The domestic deficit is more or less in the area of one billion shekels. This a little higher than our forecast, which saw a deficit of a few hundred million shekels," he said.

Finance Minister Dan Meridor has promised to examine the budget at the end of the first quarter and seek further reductions if spending looks to be running ahead of the targeted 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.
Brodett, who will be leaving his post at the end of March before any budget deliberations begin, said further spending reductions should be accompanied by an interest rate cut.
"Perhaps a (budget) cut is needed, but if we cut without immediate and complementary measures, the effectiveness of the cut will be very, very small," he said, referring to a rate cut.
Brodett said the deficit was wider than forecast because of slower-than-projected growth in tax revenues. He said tax revenues would not pick up without faster economic growth.
"In order to revive economic activity and return the economy to four percent growth or even more, the fastest and most efficient tool is monetary policy," Brodett said.
The Treasury is forecasting gross domestic product to expand four percent this year, but most private sector economists are expecting growth to be well under that figure.
Brodett said he did not think the Treasury had to keep to the 2.8 percent deficit target at all costs.
"If it's one or two tenths of a percent (over) that's a matter of fine-tuning. However, a deviation of a percentage point is not nice," he said.
